author: a. r. king
title: Carter and Taylor announce House passage of Deporting Fraudsters Act targeting benefit fraud
text:
Rep. Earl L. “Buddy” Carter announced on Mar. 18 the House passage of the Deporting Fraudsters Act, a bill introduced by Rep. Dave Taylor and co-sponsored by Carter, which aims to make non-U.S. nationals inadmissible and deportable if they are found guilty of defrauding the United States government.
The legislation is intended to address concerns about public resources being misused by individuals who are not citizens. The bill would also apply to those who unlawfully receive federal, state, or local public benefits.
“Illegal alien fraudsters are draining taxpayer dollars and taking benefits from American citizens,” said Rep. Carter. “I proudly co-sponsored the Deporting Fraudsters Act because it’s common sense: if you steal from the United States and the most vulnerable in our society, you have no right to be here. I applaud the leadership of Rep. Taylor for working to protect American citizens against waste, fraud, and abuse.”
Rep. Taylor said, “It’s a no-brainer – if an illegal alien defrauds the United States or steals benefits from our nation’s most vulnerable, they should be permanently removed from our country. Americans work too hard to have their tax dollars and benefits stolen by illegal aliens who shouldn’t be here in the first place. My Deporting Fraudsters Act will bolster the Trump Administration’s efforts to do just that, and today I’m proud to see it take a major step toward becoming law.”
Buddy Carter has served in Congress representing Georgia’s 1st district since replacing Jack Kingston in 2015 according to available information. In recent elections, Carter has consistently won re-election: he defeated Patti Hewitt in 2024 with 62% of the vote; Joyce Griggs in 2020 with 58.35%; Wade Herring in 2022 with 59.15%; Lisa Ring in 2018 with 57.8%; and Brian Reese in 2014 with 60.9%.
The next steps for the Deporting Fraudsters Act involve consideration by the Senate before it can become law.
